description: Class bound on the two-nucleon channel asymmetry: the crossing budget c = s^2 = 9 forced by the 3-strand layout caps R <= 9 against nature's 33.7, lifting the per-operator ceiling-9 to the whole single-block-exchange braid class. Audit-only; conditional on cited H1/H2; no fit.

hypotheses_cited_not_derived.H1: log|lambda| = k*log q, k integer, |k| <= c(w), extremes attained (block_transposition_lift_probe; k integral to 1.8e-22 at 90 dps)
hypotheses_cited_not_derived.H2: s = 3 strands per nucleon is FORCED (StrandLayoutForcesChain / qou-gwr9)

budget.identification: c = s^2 = Delta_{3,3}, the block transposition

result.verdict: CAPPED. With s=3 strands per nucleon (H2, forced), a single two-nucleon block exchange has c=9 inter-nucleon crossings (=s^2, which IS Delta_{3,3}). By H1 the channel log-moduli are k*log q with |k|<=c, so the achievable asymmetry is R<=9. Nature needs R=33.7055, so the single-block-exchange braid class is EXCLUDED (scope-(b), given H1+H2). Reaching R_nature would need c>=34 inter-nucleon crossings, i.e. s>=6 strands per nucleon, contradicting the forced s=3. This EXPLAINS the ceiling 9 reported for Delta_{3,3}: 9 is s^2, not a property of that one operator. Does NOT exclude repeated exchanges (Delta^m, c=9m; the minimal carrier is m=1 by the 2026-08-29 owner ruling) or non-braid carriers. Does NOT close the binding gap.
